title: finding(types): `PercentFieldMetadata` declares `precision`/`min`/`max` but NOT `scale` — and `scale` is the only one the percent cell renderer reads, so an author following the declared type silently gets zero decimals
body:
Found in the in-seat review of PR objectui#9773 (card objectui#9452), and reported by the lane that was in the file rather than left for an author to trip over. ⛔ Filed rather than folded in: it sits adjacent to a docblock that card's dispatch fenced off by name.

## What

`packages/types/src/field-types.ts:427`–`:432`:

```ts
export interface PercentFieldMetadata extends BaseFieldMetadata {
  type: 'percent';
  precision?: number;
  min?: number;
  max?: number;
}
```

**No `scale`.** And `scale` is the key the percent CELL renderer actually reads for its fraction digits — `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` takes `percentField.scale ?? 0`, deliberately, after objectui#9295 corrected it away from `precision`.

⇒ an author reading the declared type writes `precision`, and gets **zero decimal places**, silently. The one key that does anything is the one the declaration does not mention.

## Measured

| probe | reading on `c1006ed8e` |
|---|---|
| SUBJECT — `scale` declared on `PercentFieldMetadata` | **absent** (`:427`–`:432`, four members, none of them `scale`) |
| ⭐ CONTROL — is `scale` declared anywhere in this file at all | **yes**, `:409` on `NumberFieldMetadata`, with a docblock that spells the distinction out: *"Total number of digits (the `p` in a `decimal(p, s)` column). Not a display setting."* for `precision`, *"Number of decimal places to display (the `s` in a `decimal(p, s)` column)."* for `scale` |

The control is what makes the absence a reading: the vocabulary exists in this file, on a sibling type, with the exact semantics the percent renderer needs — so the percent arm's omission is a gap, ⛔ not a convention.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a two-line patch

⚠️ Adding `scale` to a published metadata interface is a **public-surface** change on `packages/types`. It is small, it is almost certainly right, and it is still a widening that owes the declaration this repo requires of one. ⛔ That is the whole reason it is not a drive-by.

⚠️ And the shape is not fully obvious: `precision` is currently declared on `PercentFieldMetadata` and, per the renderer's own settled docblock, is **not** what the renderer reads. So the card has to decide whether `scale` joins `precision` there or whether `precision` is itself a misdeclaration on this arm — and the second question is adjacent to text a landed ruling deliberately settled. ⛔ Not decided here.

## Not measured

⛔ Whether any other `*FieldMetadata` arm has the same gap — only the percent arm was read, against the number arm as a control. ⛔ Whether any first-party schema actually authors `precision` on a percent field expecting decimals; no census was run. ⛔ What the spec's own percent field face declares, which is another repo.

Refs: objectui#9452 / PR objectui#9773 (the review that surfaced it) · objectui#9295 (the landed `precision` → `scale` correction in the renderer) · `packages/types/src/field-types.ts:409` (the control).
